validated_results.reason: Prospective case-cohort study measuring first morning-void urinary melatonin metabolite (aMT6s) in cancer-free men and subsequent incident prostate cancer risk with a hazard ratio reported.

extraction.comparison_type: Morning aMT6s levels below the median versus above the median (advanced prostate cancer)
extraction.timing: prospective (baseline urinary aMT6s before incident diagnosis)
extraction.population: Icelandic men without prostate cancer nested within the AGES-Reykjavik cohort

sample_size.excerpt: We undertook a case-cohort study of 928 Icelandic men without prostate cancer (PCa) nested within the Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility (AGES)-Reykjavik cohort to investigate the prospective association between first morning-void urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (aMT6s) levels and the subsequent risk for PCa, under the hypothesis that men with lower aMT6s levels have an increased risk for advanced PCa.

cases.excerpt: A total of 111 men were diagnosed with incident PCa, including 24 with advanced disease.

effect_size.excerpt: Men with morning aMT6s levels below the median had a fourfold statistically significant increased risk for advanced disease compared with men with levels above the median (hazard ratio: 4.04; 95% confidence interval, 1.26-12.98).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Men with morning aMT6s levels below the median had a fourfold statistically significant increased risk for advanced disease compared with men with levels above the median (hazard ratio: 4.04; 95% confidence interval, 1.26-12.98).

comparison.excerpt: Men with morning aMT6s levels below the median had a fourfold statistically significant increased risk for advanced disease compared with men with levels above the median
